input.description: Payoff kind required fix
input.prompt:
You are agent P, one Opus sub-agent finishing stack 04 of the Katalyst project. Your task is small and sits on the critical path: everything that costs money waits for it.

Read first, fully, in this order:
1. /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/briefs/04-common.md  (binding)
2. /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/briefs/04-resume-common.md  (binding — the machine's resource rules)
3. /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/stack-04-generation.md — in the section "04b pull request 4", the numbered item 3, "The payoff discriminator".
4. In your worktree: AGENTS.md; backend/src/katalyst/domain/proposition.py; backend/src/katalyst/engine/client.py (`what_goes_out`, `wire_schema`); backend/src/katalyst/engine/prompt.py (`prompt_hash`); spec/generation/proposals.md and spec/generation/replay.md where they speak of the payoff shapes and the prompt fingerprint.

YOUR WORKTREE: /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/fix-04-payoff-kind  — branch fix/04-payoff-kind-required, cut from main (48eb562). Commit on it (Conventional Commits, co-author line as in 04-common.md). Do not push, do not open a pull request, touch no other worktree. Run `npm ci` in frontend/ once if you need the browser tooling (you will, for the generated types).

THE DEFECT. `ContractPayoff.kind` and `PricePayoff.kind` in domain/proposition.py have defaults (`= "contract"`, `= "price"`). The coordinator measured today, on main, what actually goes out over the wire (`katalyst.engine.client.what_goes_out()`): ContractPayoff `required` = [venue, contract_id, title, side]; PricePayoff `required` = [instrument, direction, move]; `kind` is in NEITHER, and its description reads "{const: contract, default: contract}". So a model may leave out the one field that tells the two payoff shapes apart, and the union `Payoff = Annotated[ContractPayoff | PricePayoff, Field(discriminator="kind")]` then cannot be read. A shape must make the wrong answer impossible rather than hope (trap (a) in 04-common.md).

THE FIX. Drop both defaults so `kind` is required. Fix every construction site — fixtures, tests, engine code, evals are NOT on this branch — and anything in frontend/ that builds a payoff once the generated types make `kind` required. Add or extend the wire-schema test so it shows `kind` in `required` on both payoff shapes AS SENT (through `wire_schema`/`what_goes_out`, not the pydantic model's own schema — lesson 15). Regenerate the browser's types (`make types` from the repo root; read the Makefile first) and confirm the diff to frontend/src/api/schema.ts is only what this change explains. If any spec chapter or decision record states the default or lists required fields, make it true (spec = kept true; a decision record gets a dated note, never a rewrite).

WHAT THIS BREAKS ON PURPOSE, AND WHAT YOU MUST NOT DO ABOUT IT. The prompt fingerprint covers the shapes as sent, so it WILL change (it is 1c224cc32fb0e3f3… on main — print the new one in your report). Therefore: (a) the boundary tests under backend/tests/boundary/ match recorded requests on their body, so the five really-recorded cassettes under backend/tests/cassettes/ will stop matching, and the four hand-made ones are derived from them (backend/tests/boundary/remake_handmade_cassettes.py); (b) any recording under backend/recordings/ would go stale (there is none on this branch). YOU NEVER RECORD ANYTHING AND NEVER HOLD A KEY. Do not edit a cassette by hand to make a test pass. Instead: make everything else green, and tell the coordinator exactly which tests fail only for want of re-recorded cassettes, and the exact commands, in order, the coordinator must run to re-record and then remake the hand-made ones (read the Makefile's `record-cassettes` target and the remake script, and say what each costs in calls if you can tell). Check whether the remake script or any cassette-related code itself constructs a payoff without `kind`.

Also check, and report in one paragraph: the first Hormuz recording showed three real refusals coded `market_without_payoff`. Read how a proposal with `claim_kind: market` and a payoff missing its `kind` would travel through engine/ today — would it surface as `market_without_payoff`, as an unreadable answer (`AnswerWeCouldNotRead`), or something else? The recording is at /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/feat-04b-recordings/backend/recordings/hormuz.jsonl (read-only for you). This tells Kent whether the defect has already bitten.

KEEP IT SMALL. This is a two-line change with a tail of call sites. No refactor, no new abstraction, nothing the defect does not force.

VERIFY (within the resource rules): targeted test files directly; `uv run ruff check .`, `uv run ruff format --check .`, both mypy runs named in 04-common.md, `npm run lint` and the type check in frontend/ directly; ONE whole server suite through the queue, in the background: `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/scripts/heavy.sh "P: server suite" -- bash -c 'cd /Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst-wt/fix-04-payoff-kind/backend && env -u ANTHROPIC_API_KEY -u FRED_API_KEY uv run pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -40'` — it may wait up to half an hour behind a browser run; draft your report meanwhile. Expect the cassette tests to fail and nothing else.

Report in the format of 04-common.md, with the line "what the coordinator must run to check you" at the top, the old and new fingerprint, and the list of tests that wait on re-recording.

I've read the four docs plus `AGENTS.md`, the stack-04 plan, Kent's decisions note (G1–G13, S1–S8), the shared agent brief and `land.sh`, and checked the repo against them. It matches the resume note. `main` is `48eb562`, no pull requests are open, the four worktrees are clean, and nothing was left running.

Five Opus agents are now running, and one browser repeat bar is in flight. Nothing has merged yet and no money has been spent this session.

## What remains of stack 04

Ten pull requests are merged. Four local branches are left, then a short tail.

| # | Branch | State | What's left |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `fix/04-vanishing-wire` | Fixed, root cause shown | Its last bar (40× at 1, 3 and 6 workers), an independent review, the pull request, then land. |
| 2 | `feat/04a-growth` (the growing-map screen) | Reviewed twice | Rebase, then 20 cold runs on a quiet machine with the log kept. Two earlier failures are still unexplained. Then the pull request and land. |
| 3 | `feat/04b-evals` | Evals done, spread engine done | The spread's chapter sweep. The path product moved into `domain/` and onto the world. A diff row that says which half of "unchanged" failed. The final `ARCHITECTURE.md`/PRD/README sweep. The payoff `kind` defaults (item 6). An independent review, then `make eval` run by me. |
| 4 | `feat/04b-recordings` | Hormuz recorded | Record `midterms`, `export-controls` and `photonics`. This was held until item 6 was settled. |

The tail is the browser wiring for `pathProduct` and the which-half field, then milestone M4 where you look at a live and a replayed map, then close-out.

## Item 6 is now its own pull request, first

Item 6 is dropping the defaults on the payoff `kind` field. The open question was whether that moves the prompt fingerprint. I measured the shape as it goes out, with no key. `kind` is not in `required` on either payoff shape, so the fingerprint will move, and the Hormuz recording and the cassettes go stale.

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

1	# Roadmap — stacks 04 to 07, through to a finished prototype
2	
3	*(The file keeps its old name so nothing that points at it breaks. Stack 03 is merged; stack 04 has its own plan.)*
4	
5	Less detailed than the plans for stacks 01, 02 and 03, on purpose: what you learn building those will change these. **Before starting each stack, rewrite its section here into a full plan file of its own**, in the style of `stack-02-schema.md` — goal, what the stack must not do, a table of pull requests with branch → base, the details that matter, a pre-decisions table, a checkable "done when", and a closing section on sub-agents and waves.
6	
7	Every stack follows the same pattern: a docs-only bottom pull request with the spec chapters → Kent reads it → code → `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated → `STATUS.md` appended. Kent builds through milestones rather than stopping at gates: code above the docs pull request proceeds while he reads.
8	
9	---
10	
11	## Stacks 03a and 03b — merged 2026-09-17
12	
13	Both are on `main` (pull requests #18, #19, #24, #25 and #21, #22, #26, #27). Their plans, `stack-03a-engine.md` and `stack-03b-canvas.md`, are history now — kept for the pattern.
14	
15	- **The engine (03a)** folds a branch onto a map, works the likelihoods through two thousand versions of the map times eight worlds, says what moved between two worlds, and answers over three routes: `POST /api/worlds`, `/api/worlds/diff`, `/api/worlds/conditional`. 259 server tests; the rules layer at 100%.
16	- **The canvas (03b)** draws the Hormuz map with encoded wires, a persistent Inspector, a two-world overlay, the six buttons, the whole keyboard, an outline view, and one keyboard-only end-to-end test. 177 browser tests.
17	- **What they did not do, on purpose: meet.** The canvas still reads the stored example and shows every computed number as an absence with a reason. Joining them is the first code of stack 04.
18	
19	---
20	
21	## Stack 04 — generation — expanded into its own plan: `stack-04-generation.md`
22	
23	**Current.** It needs seven pull requests and a stack is capped at four, so it runs as two parallel stacks, the way 03a ∥ 03b did:
24	
25	- **04a — the browser.** Join the canvas to the three world routes (no model needed; real computed numbers on screen first), then the map drawing itself from a stream.
26	- **04b — the server.** Five `spec/generation/` chapters and decision record 0015; the one-proposal-per-call pipeline; the event stream, transcripts and **replay mode (record 0012, accepted 2026-09-17)**; evals, the ensemble, and the provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths.
27	
28	**Kent answered its open questions on 2026-09-17** (`notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`): no ensemble — the stated range, labelled (record 0015); "This happened" fixed by counting only surviving versions; up to three silent retries after a refusal; $500 for the stack with a $15 hard stop per run; Hormuz recorded early, all four once the prompt is frozen.
29	
30	**Before any code that calls Claude: load the `claude-api` skill.** Decision record 0006 holds the verified specifics; never write a model name, a parameter or a price from memory.
31	
32	---
33	
34	## Stack 05 — the thesis (needs 04)
35	
36	**Goal:** the map compiles into something a trader can act on.
37	
38	**Rests on:** decision record 0010 (Polymarket and FRED for outside data). **Chapters:** all of `spec/thesis/`.
39	
40	| Pull request | Contents |
41	|--------------|----------|
42	| Chapters | The five thesis chapters |
43	| Deriving the stop-loss | From the sensitivity sweep: the claim whose flip hurts a terminal most, **filtered** to claims that resolve *before* the terminal and are *publicly observable* (invariant INV-14). That claim is the stop-loss. Take-profit is the mirror image. Claims that matter but cannot be watched in time are listed as "unhedgeable" — never used as a stop |
44	| Tails and distribution | The tail strip: rare, large outcomes each on their own row with a suggested hedge, **never averaged away**. From the random runs: 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile outcomes; the average loss in the worst 5% of runs; the chance of being wiped out. **Read these off the pooled worlds — both loops together, all 16 000 — and say so on the card**, because a payoff distribution is honestly about how the dice fall *and* how sure we are of the inputs, unlike a belief's range, which is only the second (decision record 0014) |
45	| Outside data | One small interface, `GroundingSource`, with a disk cache. Decision record **0013** sets the division: a `payoff` on a `market` claim names *what you would trade* — a `ContractPayoff` (venue, the venue's own contract identifier, title, and the side: `yes` or `no`) or a `PricePayoff` (instrument, `long` or `short`, and `move` as a fraction). What it **costs** — price, spread, and when we looked — is never on the payoff; it is a `market` belief fetched live. Polymarket (no key needed). # Roadmap — stacks 04 to 07, through to a finished prototype

*(The file keeps its old name so nothing that points at it breaks. Stack 03 is merged; stack 04 has its own plan.)*

Less detailed than the plans for stacks 01, 02 and 03, on purpose: what you learn building those will change these. **Before starting each stack, rewrite its section here into a full plan file of its own**, in the style of `stack-02-schema.md` — goal, what the stack must not do, a table of pull requests with branch → base, the details that matter, a pre-decisions table, a checkable "done when", and a closing section on sub-agents and waves.

Every stack follows the same pattern: a docs-only bottom pull request with the spec chapters → Kent reads it → code → `ARCHITECTURE.md` updated → `STATUS.md` appended. Kent builds through milestones rather than stopping at gates: code above the docs pull request proceeds while he reads.

---

## Stacks 03a and 03b — merged 2026-09-17

Both are on `main` (pull requests #18, #19, #24, #25 and #21, #22, #26, #27). Their plans, `stack-03a-engine.md` and `stack-03b-canvas.md`, are history now — kept for the pattern.

- **The engine (03a)** folds a branch onto a map, works the likelihoods through two thousand versions of the map times eight worlds, says what moved between two worlds, and answers over three routes: `POST /api/worlds`, `/api/worlds/diff`, `/api/worlds/conditional`. 259 server tests; the rules layer at 100%.
- **The canvas (03b)** draws the Hormuz map with encoded wires, a persistent Inspector, a two-world overlay, the six buttons, the whole keyboard, an outline view, and one keyboard-only end-to-end test. 177 browser tests.
- **What they did not do, on purpose: meet.** The canvas still reads the stored example and shows every computed number as an absence with a reason. Joining them is the first code of stack 04.

---

## Stack 04 — generation — expanded into its own plan: `stack-04-generation.md`

**Current.** It needs seven pull requests and a stack is capped at four, so it runs as two parallel stacks, the way 03a ∥ 03b did:

- **04a — the browser.** Join the canvas to the three world routes (no model needed; real computed numbers on screen first), then the map drawing itself from a stream.
- **04b — the server.** Five `spec/generation/` chapters and decision record 0015; the one-proposal-per-call pipeline; the event stream, transcripts and **replay mode (record 0012, accepted 2026-09-17)**; evals, the ensemble, and the provenance-derived spread on arrow strengths.

**Kent answered its open questions on 2026-09-17** (`notes/2026-09-17-kent-decisions-stack-04.md`): no ensemble — the stated range, labelled (record 0015); "This happened" fixed by counting only surviving versions; up to three silent retries after a refusal; $500 for the stack with a $15 hard stop per run; Hormuz recorded early, all four once the prompt is frozen.

**Before any code that calls Claude: load the `claude-api` skill.** Decision record 0006 holds the verified specifics; never write a model name, a parameter or a price from memory.

---

## Stack 05 — the thesis (needs 04)

**Goal:** the map compiles into something a trader can act on.

**Rests on:** decision record 0010 (Polymarket and FRED for outside data). **Chapters:** all of `spec/thesis/`.

| Pull request | Contents |
|--------------|----------|
| Chapters | The five thesis chapters |
| Deriving the stop-loss | From the sensitivity sweep: the claim whose flip hurts a terminal most, **filtered** to claims that resolve *before* the terminal and are *publicly observable* (invariant INV-14). That claim is the stop-loss. Take-profit is the mirror image. Claims that matter but cannot be watched in time are listed as "unhedgeable" — never used as a stop |
| Tails and distribution | The tail strip: rare, large outcomes each on their own row with a suggested hedge, **never averaged away**. From the random runs: 10th, 50th, and 90th percentile outcomes; the average loss in the worst 5% of runs; the chance of being wiped out. **Read these off the pooled worlds — both loops together, all 16 000 — and say so on the card**, because a payoff distribution is honestly about how the dice fall *and* how sure we are of the inputs, unlike a belief's range, which is only the second (decision record 0014) |
| Outside data | One small interface, `GroundingSource`, with a disk cache. FRED (free key; **its attribution sentence must appear on screen** — requirement FR-26 has the wording). Market prices fill the `market` belief slot. When two venues disagree, show both; never average |

Open question in the requirements: mirror the multi-leg structures prediction markets already use, or a simpler list of legs plus conditions. Decide in `strategy-export.md` and tell Kent |

1	# Midpoint review: finish the reasoning loop and simplify its mathematics
2	
3	**Date:** 2026-09-21. **Status:** recommendation for Kent's review; no product code or accepted decisions changed.
4	
5	## Recommendation
6	
7	Keep the workbench, evidence Inspector, immutable branches, comparison, typed API, and pure domain boundary. Rebuild the quantitative contract around **small explicit models and conditional trade theses**. Finish one complete, keyless Hormuz journey before extending simulation, refinement, probes, or market coverage.
8	
9	The project's central idea fits the assignment well. Its engineering discipline is substantial. The main problem is that the mathematics and feature requirements have grown beyond the evidence supporting them, while the final thesis/strategy experience remains unfinished. Some issues are actual calculation defects, not matters of taste or insufficient disclaimers.
10	
11	Kent's stated priorities during this review were: **no fixed deadline; a compelling, complete demo with defensible assumptions; reconsider the quantitative design from the ground up when it adds apparent certainty rather than useful information.** This proposal follows those priorities. It recommends a bounded redesign, with a specific completion gate, rather than a broad research program.
12	
13	## How the independent review was conducted
14	
15	Four assignment-first passes were frozen before reading the initial brainstorming or existing design. They covered product, probability/causality, finance, and the primary reviewer's synthesis. Each subsequent audit began with `docs/initial-brainstorming.md`, then examined the specs, decisions, implementation, and history. External research used selected primary literature and the assignment's named inspiration sources.
16	
17	Three parallel reviewers used `gpt-5.6-sol`, the available successor to the requested but unavailable `gpt-5-sol`. Their findings were checked and reconciled; the final recommendation below is a synthesis, not a vote or concatenation of reports.
18	
19	The implementation review distinguishes merged `main` (`0df6c23`) from the unmerged browser (`3433266` plus dirty changes), generation (`8261053` plus dirty changes), and observation-fix (`6ee387c` plus a dirty test) worktrees. The newer work already implements much of generation and engine–canvas integration. Recommendations account for it. These are working-tree snapshots, not a claim about the current status of remote pull requests.

24

40	| 5 | Evaluate semantic quality and time to useful output | Directs future work toward better reasoning and usability, rather than more graph structure |
41	
42	These changes reinforce one another. A smaller model needs fewer parameters to defend, fewer generated claims to research, fewer UI states to explain, and a smaller acceptance suite. The saved effort goes into the thesis and evidence.
43

45	
46	### Observation is mathematically wrong in a tiny case

48	Let `P(A)=0.20`, `P(B|A)=0.90`, and `P(B|not A)=0.10`. Observing B should yield `P(A|B)=9/13`, approximately 69%. The current engine returns 20%, unchanged. The primary reviewer independently reproduced the result.
49	
50	The uncommitted observation test adds another warning sign: it requires movement across a zero-strength arrow, where the declared independent model implies no update. Finite sampling noise has become expected behavior. Details and reproduction: [probability audit](06-probability-audit.md).
51	
52	### The event semantics alter the requested scenario
53	
54	The brief's “Hormuz opens, then Iran is struck” permits both events to occur. A later strike can reduce sustained shipping, increase the risk premium, or reverse the financial conclusion. 55	
56	Use distinct dated claims: opening occurred; strike occurred; shipping remains usable through a later date. This makes the story and its arithmetic easier to understand.
57	
58	### Path products and uncertainty bands overstate what is known
59	
60	The Verify path product multiplies dependent marginal probabilities. If Y always equals X and both have probability 0.5, the product is 0.25 while the conjunction is 0.5. The product is neither a general joint probability nor a conservative bound. Remove it.
61	
62	The nested simulation samples a distribution fitted to model-stated probability ranges while holding important parameters and structure fixed. That can explore a declared mathematical distribution, but it does not add evidence. The variance correction does not generally recover its advertised quantiles. A later Brier score on a binary outcome cannot validate an interval over that event's latent probability; the event resolves to true or false, not to its probability.
63	
64	The literature supports distinguishing these objects. Proper scores assess specified predictive quantities; numerical outcome intervals and intervals over unknown probability parameters need different validation designs. [Gneiting and Raftery, 2007](https://doi.org/10.1198/016214506000001437). The audit also identifies mistaken transfers from FermiEval, QuantSightBench, and the forecast-consistency literature into the current ADR rationale.
65	
66	## The proposed quantitative contract
67	
68	**The broad map is a set of causal hypotheses. Quantify a small, complete portion only when doing so helps answer a decision question.**
69	
70	For the showcase, use a small acyclic graph of dated binary claims, normally with at most two direct causes per claim. Record an explicit conditional probability for each parent combination. 71	
72	The causal interpretation remains an assumption: the selected parents and mechanisms must be adequate for the proposed intervention. Exact arithmetic cannot identify real-world effects from generated text. [Pearl, causal intervention semantics](https://bayes.cs.ucla.edu/BOOK-2K/ch3-3.pdf).
73	
74	Show model-implied probabilities, endpoint changes, and results under a few named coherent assumption sets. The spread across those sets is a sensitivity envelope over what was tested. Store user assumptions separately from the model's, and let the user explicitly choose which assumption set a calculation uses; never blend owners silently.
75	
76	An unquantified dependency blocks numerical propagation through it. It may still have a useful mechanism explanation. Reachability tells us which claims may be affected; it does not by itself determine direction or magnitude. Do not hide a model-generated revision behind a deterministic-looking animation.
77	
78	The worked alternative in [09-worked-quantitative-alternative.md](09-worked-quantitative-alternative.md) demonstrates both assignment use cases with four variables. 79	
80	**A table is not automatically better evidence than a log-odds coefficient.** The reason to prefer this design is transparent meaning, exact small-case arithmetic, and lower implementation complexity. The model decision experiment has to test this, not assume it away.
81	
82	## Make the thesis financially meaningful
83	
84	The planned “model minus market equals edge” feature is unsafe when the model number assumes the hypothesis is true and the quote spans all possible outcomes. This is a design risk before the thesis stack is implemented, not an allegation that shipped code already calculates this trade signal.
85	
86	In the worked alternative, buying a hypothetical $1 binary payout at $0.40 with $0.02 flat costs loses an expected $0.07 under the full model. 87	
88	The thesis should identify the instrument/exposure, side, horizon, entry condition, current or recorded quote, key assumptions, conditional consequences, and exit logic. Separate:
89	
90	- **Thesis invalidation:** evidence a causal premise failed.
91	- **Offsetting shock:** something else overwhelms the trade while the mechanism remains valid.
92	- **Risk exit:** the user's loss, price, or time rule.
93	- **Execution instruction:** how an order would be submitted and what it can actually guarantee.
94	
95	A sensitivity sweep can suggest monitoring conditions. It cannot derive a guaranteed stop-loss or automatically identify a logical falsifier. Terminal outcomes also cannot establish drawdown or stop-trigger behavior. See the [finance audit](07-finance-audit.md).
96	
97	Use named stresses and conditional losses where calculable. Keep “no positive edge at this price” and “conditional thesis; missing quote” as complete, useful results.
98	
99	## Preserve the software investment; change its center of gravity
100	
101	Keep the existing language/framework choices, generated schema boundary, graph validation, immutable patches, local diffs, keyboard support, provenance receipts, and replay transport. 102	
103	The current priority should be an integrated branch, a reviewed replay, and the thesis dock. The newest backend and browser worktrees do not yet prove the full journey together. 104

106	
107	Move endpoint names and build diagnostics into Run details. Preserve analysis dates and recorded/live labels in the main flow. 108	
109	## Evidence and testing should challenge the model
110	
111	Source retrieval currently establishes that a URL appeared in the search response. It does not establish that the article supports a probability, timing assumption, effect size, or instrument mapping. Attach a passage or locator, its support role, and the model's explanation of relevance. Verify the trade-critical sources in the showcase by hand. 112	
113	Keep structural and property tests. Add small independent mathematical oracles and a short human content rubric. 118	|---|---|

120	| Merged frontend | Lint/type checks passed; 176 tests passed, 1 skipped |
121	| New browser working tree | Checks passed; 260 tests passed |

<result>## VERDICT: READY AFTER MUST-FIX

The diagnosis is right and the new end-to-end test has real teeth. But the hook's stop condition is not the fact the docstring claims it is, and in this app it never becomes true — so the fix works only because it polls the library forever. That has to be corrected before it lands, especially since it is about to be rebased together with `feat/04a-growth`.

---

## MUST FIX BEFORE MERGE

### 1. `frontend/src/graph/Canvas.tsx:160` — the stop condition never fires; the asking never stops

**What is wrong.** `useNodesInitialized()` with its default options does **not** report handle bounds, and in this app it is permanently `false`. So `useHandlesTheLibraryHasMeasured` creates a 120 ms interval on mount and clears it only on unmount (or when the tile list changes, when it immediately makes another). The map forces a full re-measure of every tile ~8 times a second for the life of the page.

**How I know** (all read in the installed `@xyflow/react@12.11.6` / `@xyflow/system@0.0.82`, plus one probe I ran):

- `node_modules/@xyflow/react/dist/esm/index.mjs:4218-4221` — with the default `includeHiddenNodes: false` the selector returns `s.nodesInitialized` and never looks at `handleBounds`. (Only the `includeHiddenNodes: true` branch checks `internals.handleBounds`.)
- `node_modules/@xyflow/system/dist/esm/index.js:1671-1717` (`adoptUserNodes`) — `nodesInitialized` is computed from `internalNode.measured.width/height` alone, and a rebuilt internal node re-seeds `measured` from `userNode.measured`, which `toFlow` never sets (it sets `initialWidth`/`initialHeight`, `toFlow.ts:214`).
- `node_modules/@xyflow/react/dist/esm/index.mjs:3482-3499` — the store's `updateNodeInternals` ends in `set({})`; it never recomputes `nodesInitialized`. `setNodes` (`:3428-3457`) is the only writer, and `StoreUpdater` (`:281-320`) calls it only when the `nodes` **prop identity** changes — at which point `Canvas.tsx:245-266` has always built brand-new node objects, so `checkEquality` cannot preserve `measured`.
- `triggerNodeChanges` (`:3550`) only writes measurements back when `hasDefaultNodes` is true or `onNodesChange` is given; `Canvas.tsx:678-680` gives neither.

I ran a probe against the real `adoptUserNodes` (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kentgang-git3-katalyst/b70a1857-a894-4bbe-b3a6-4d7cf3ebc4f8/scratchpad/reviews/wire/probe.mjs`):

```
1. first setNodes (as Canvas builds them)          -> nodesInitialized: false | handleBounds: undefined
2. next setNodes, new objects (hover/selection)    -> nodesInitialized: false | handleBounds: undefined   (measurement discarded)
4. setNodes, same objects, after measurement       -> nodesInitialized: true  | handleBounds: undefined   <-- true WITHOUT handle bounds
```

Row 4 falsifies "false until every tile has handle bounds" outright. Row 2 shows why it can never turn true here.

**Cost, per tick, forever:** one `querySelector` per tile, then `getDimensions` + `getBoundingClientRect` on the tile and on each of its four sockets (`system:939` `getHandleBounds`), plus `getComputedStyle` on the viewport — roughly 5N forced layout reads for N tiles — and a new internal node object for every tile, which re-renders every `NodeWrapper`. On a 20-tile growing map that is ~100 forced layout reads and 20 React re-renders 8 times a second, permanently. I proved the loop and the work; I did **not** measure wall-clock cost.

**Smallest fix.** Ask for the fact that actually means "the sockets have been measured", and bound the asking:

```ts
// The option is named for hidden nodes, but it is the only branch of this hook
// that looks at handle bounds at all — see the library's own selector.
const EVERY_TILE_MEASURED = { includeHiddenNodes: true } as const;
const measured = useNodesInitialized(EVERY_TILE_MEASURED);
```

That branch walks the live `nodeLookup`, so it re-evaluates on the `set({})` the forced measurement produces, and `nodeHasDimensions` is already satisfied by #37's `initialWidth`/`initialHeight`. Add a bounded number of attempts (about 25, ~3 s) so a tile that can never be measured — a hidden one gets `handleBounds: undefined` written deliberately at `react:3450`-ish in `updateNodeInternals` — cannot hold a timer for the life of the page. (No tile is `hidden` today; on `feat/04a-growth` unplaced tiles are filtered out of the array rather than hidden, so this is insurance, not a present bug.)

### 2. `frontend/src/graph/Canvas.tsx:136-173` and the commit message — the explanation says three things that are not true

- *"`nodesInitialized` is that fact — false until every tile has handle bounds"* — false; see probe row 4.
- *"The asking stops the moment the library says it has measured"* — it never stops.
- *"It is a timer rather than an animation frame because a browser produces no frames while nothing is changing"* — `useUpdateNodeInternals` itself defers the whole update to `requestAnimationFrame` (`react:3940`), so the fix already rides on a frame; the timer supplies only the repetition. (`setInterval` is throttled in a background tab too, so it is not the escape the sentence implies.)

This is Kent's second veto — not knowing why it did that — and the house rule that a word must mean what it says. Fix the words in the same change as the code, and fix the commit message when the branch is re-committed.

---

## SHOULD FIX

### 3. One rule, not two: the sockets can be declared, exactly as #37 declared the box

`getEdgePosition` falls back to `toHandleBounds(node.handles)` when `internals.handleBounds` is missing, and `isNodeInitialized` (`system:1429`) accepts `node.handles?.length` together with `node.initialWidth`. So if `toFlow` gave each tile its `handles` the way it already gives it `initialWidth`/`initialHeight`, **the wires would be drawable on the first frame with no measurement and no polling at all**, and the file would carry one rule — *every tile is told its box and where its sockets sit, from the one place that worked them out* — instead of a declaration plus a repair loop. It would also be pinnable by a pure-data vitest test in the shape of `src/graph/__tests__/measured.test.ts`, and it matches `spec/workbench/layout-and-zoom.md:50` ("never measured off the screen — so layout stays a pure function").

Two honest caveats, which is why I am not making this a must-fix: the socket geometry lives only in `tile.css:477-494` (8 × 6 px, `left/right: -8px`, `top: 38%`/`62%`, `translateY(-50%)`), so declaring it in TypeScript duplicates a number unless the CSS is driven from the same constants; and `parseHandles` (`system:1639-1647`) rebuilds bounds from the declared handles on **every** `adoptUserNodes`, so a wrong declared offset would move a wire's ends on every hover, not just once. Worth putting to Kent as a design choice rather than deciding here.

### 4. No component-level test pins the rule; one is practical

The diff adds no vitest test. Existing tests already render inside `ReactFlowProvider` (`src/graph/wires/__tests__/causalWire.test.tsx`, `src/components/__tests__/tile.test.tsx`), so a jsdom test that renders `<ReactFlow>` with nodes carrying `measured` and asserts the asking **stops** is straightforward — and it fails on the code as it stands, which is exactly the pin this needs. If the fix goes the way of item 3 instead, the test is pure data and even simpler.

### 5. `frontend/e2e/hormuz.spec.ts:389` — on the ordinary path only one arrow is ever checked

Outside the new shimmed test, the only arrow asserted to be on the glass is `H->C`, through `openThePanelOnTheArrow` at line 863. A different vanished arrow would still go unnoticed in an ordinary cold run. Add the eight-by-name assertion (the one already written at lines 970-980) right after `waitForTheLayout(page, 7)` in the stored-example test — it costs nothing and closes the blind spot for every run, not just the shimmed one.

### 6. For the rebase with `feat/04a-growth`

- That branch's `nodes` memo uses `flatMap` and **drops** tiles with no position yet (`feat-04a-growth/frontend/src/graph/Canvas.tsx:276-309`), so `everyTile` built from `drawing.nodes` will name tiles that are not on the glass. Harmless (`useUpdateNodeInternals` skips ids it cannot find in the DOM) but the docstring's "Every tile on the glass" stops being true. Build the list from the `nodes` the surface actually hands over.
- Every arriving claim changes `drawing`, so the effect restarts and fires one immediate forced re-measure of the whole map per arrival — on top of the permanent poll. That branch's own comment at `Canvas.tsx:450-454` calls re-delivering sizes per arrival *"the storm that starved the drawing library's own measuring"*. Fixing item 1 removes the poll; the per-arrival re-measure is fine and probably wanted.

### 7. `Canvas.tsx:194-197` — `everyTile` churns more than it needs to

`drawing` is recomputed whenever `heights` changes (opening or closing a branch), so `everyTile` is a new array even when the identifiers are identical, and the effect restarts. Comparing the joined identifiers, or keying the memo on something stable, would make the comment "held still so that the asking does not restart on every render" true in more cases.

---

## NITS

- `Canvas.tsx:159` — `useHandlesTheLibraryHasMeasured` uses the drawing library's word. `spec/vocabulary.md:73` says the project's word for where a wire attaches is **port**, and `tiles-ports-wires.md` calls them sockets on screen. The docstring does explain "handle", so this is house-style rather than a rule break.
- `Canvas.tsx:169,170` — `[...ids]` copies the array on every call; only the `readonly` type needs it.
- `e2e/hormuz.spec.ts:305-311` — "the waiting is gone" overstates it: `toHaveCount` is auto-retrying and still waits, up to the config's 15 s `expect.timeout`. The comment's "fifteen seconds" is right; the sentence before it is not.
- `frontend/playwright.config.ts` on this branch still uses fixed ports 8015/5187 with `reuseExistingServer`. Lesson 18's fix rides on `feat/04a-growth`, so whoever runs this branch's last repeat bar must not run it as-is — a bar is on those ports in this worktree right now.

---

## What I checked and found sound

**Proved by reading the installed library:**

- **The root cause is right.** `EdgeWrapper` returns `null` — no `.react-flow__edge` element at all — when `getEdgePosition` is null (`react:2974`), and `getEdgePosition` is null when a node has no handle bounds and no declared handles (`system:1424-1440`). Handle bounds are written only by `updateNodeInternals`, reached either from the `ResizeObserver` (`react:2147-2171`) or from `useUpdateNodeInternals`; the `Handle` component registers nothing itself. So "tiles all present, arrows gone" is exactly the signature of a dropped tile notification, and #37's `initialWidth`/`initialHeight` is precisely why the tiles stay visible while the wires do not.
- **Nothing already placed moves.** Positions come from our own layout and `updateAbsolutePositions` recomputes them identically; the node extent is infinite so nothing is clamped; `NodeWrapper`'s inline size comes from `node.width/height`, not from `measured` (`react:2360-2365`). A forced re-measure cannot make anything jump.
- **Unmount is clean.** The interval is cleared; the in-flight `requestAnimationFrame` inside `useUpdateNodeInternals` is harmless because the store action early-returns with no viewport element.
- **No ResizeObserver feedback loop.** The forced updates do not change any element's size, so they cannot feed the observer. (They do add load, which is item 1's concern, not a loop.)
- **No fight with the keyboard rule from #36/#37.** The poll re-renders `NodeWrapper` but React keeps the same DOM element, so focus is never dropped to the page and `mayLandAgain` is never put in the "nowhere" state by it. Read, not run in a browser.

**Proved by running:**

- `npx biome check src/graph/Canvas.tsx e2e/hormuz.spec.ts` — clean.
- `npx vitest run src/graph` — 13 files, 114 tests, green.
- The `adoptUserNodes` probe above.

**Checked and found in order:**

- The new end-to-end test is deterministic and would be red without the fix: its shim drops every tile's notification and keeps the glass's, so with no repair path no handle bounds are ever written and all eight edges are absent. It asserts both the count and the eight arrows **by name**, so "some arrows drew" cannot pass.
- The old tolerance in `openThePanelOnTheArrow` — the loop that swallowed "the arrow was not on the glass at all" for 45 s — is genuinely gone and replaced by a named assertion.
- No spec chapter or `ARCHITECTURE.md` sentence is made false by this change. #37's rule was never written into the spec (it lives only in `toFlow.ts`'s comment and `measured.test.ts`), so nothing about handles needs a chapter today. If item 3 is taken, `spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md` §"The ports" deserves one sentence saying the sockets' places are declared, not discovered.
- The branch is one commit on `48eb562`, the worktree is clean, and it touches only the two files RESUME lists.

**What I did not do:** no browser, no Playwright, no repeat bar, no whole suite; I did not measure the wall-clock or CPU cost of the poll, only proved that it runs forever and counted the DOM work per tick.</result>

<result>## VERDICT: READY AFTER MUST-FIX

The diagnosis is right and the new end-to-end test has real teeth. But the hook's stop condition is not the fact the docstring claims it is, and in this app it never becomes true — so the fix works only because it polls the library forever. That has to be corrected before it lands, especially since it is about to be rebased together with `feat/04a-growth`.

---

## MUST FIX BEFORE MERGE

### 1. `frontend/src/graph/Canvas.tsx:160` — the stop condition never fires; the asking never stops

**What is wrong.** `useNodesInitialized()` with its default options does **not** report handle bounds, and in this app it is permanently `false`. So `useHandlesTheLibraryHasMeasured` creates a 120 ms interval on mount and clears it only on unmount (or when the tile list changes, when it immediately makes another). The map forces a full re-measure of every tile ~8 times a second for the life of the page.

**How I know** (all read in the installed `@xyflow/react@12.11.6` / `@xyflow/system@0.0.82`, plus one probe I ran):

- `node_modules/@xyflow/react/dist/esm/index.mjs:4218-4221` — with the default `includeHiddenNodes: false` the selector returns `s.nodesInitialized` and never looks at `handleBounds`. (Only the `includeHiddenNodes: true` branch checks `internals.handleBounds`.)
- `node_modules/@xyflow/system/dist/esm/index.js:1671-1717` (`adoptUserNodes`) — `nodesInitialized` is computed from `internalNode.measured.width/height` alone, and a rebuilt internal node re-seeds `measured` from `userNode.measured`, which `toFlow` never sets (it sets `initialWidth`/`initialHeight`, `toFlow.ts:214`).
- `node_modules/@xyflow/react/dist/esm/index.mjs:3482-3499` — the store's `updateNodeInternals` ends in `set({})`; it never recomputes `nodesInitialized`. `setNodes` (`:3428-3457`) is the only writer, and `StoreUpdater` (`:281-320`) calls it only when the `nodes` **prop identity** changes — at which point `Canvas.tsx:245-266` has always built brand-new node objects, so `checkEquality` cannot preserve `measured`.
- `triggerNodeChanges` (`:3550`) only writes measurements back when `hasDefaultNodes` is true or `onNodesChange` is given; `Canvas.tsx:678-680` gives neither.

I ran a probe against the real `adoptUserNodes` (`/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-kentgang-git3-katalyst/b70a1857-a894-4bbe-b3a6-4d7cf3ebc4f8/scratchpad/reviews/wire/probe.mjs`):

```
1. first setNodes (as Canvas builds them)          -> nodesInitialized: false | handleBounds: undefined
2. next setNodes, new objects (hover/selection)    -> nodesInitialized: false | handleBounds: undefined   (measurement discarded)
4. setNodes, same objects, after measurement       -> nodesInitialized: true  | handleBounds: undefined   <-- true WITHOUT handle bounds
```

Row 4 falsifies "false until every tile has handle bounds" outright. Row 2 shows why it can never turn true here.

**Cost, per tick, forever:** one `querySelector` per tile, then `getDimensions` + `getBoundingClientRect` on the tile and on each of its four sockets (`system:939` `getHandleBounds`), plus `getComputedStyle` on the viewport — roughly 5N forced layout reads for N tiles — and a new internal node object for every tile, which re-renders every `NodeWrapper`. On a 20-tile growing map that is ~100 forced layout reads and 20 React re-renders 8 times a second, permanently. I proved the loop and the work; I did **not** measure wall-clock cost.

**Smallest fix.** Ask for the fact that actually means "the sockets have been measured", and bound the asking:

```ts
// The option is named for hidden nodes, but it is the only branch of this hook
// that looks at handle bounds at all — see the library's own selector.
const EVERY_TILE_MEASURED = { includeHiddenNodes: true } as const;
const measured = useNodesInitialized(EVERY_TILE_MEASURED);
```

That branch walks the live `nodeLookup`, so it re-evaluates on the `set({})` the forced measurement produces, and `nodeHasDimensions` is already satisfied by #37's `initialWidth`/`initialHeight`. Add a bounded number of attempts (about 25, ~3 s) so a tile that can never be measured — a hidden one gets `handleBounds: undefined` written deliberately at `react:3450`-ish in `updateNodeInternals` — cannot hold a timer for the life of the page. (No tile is `hidden` today; on `feat/04a-growth` unplaced tiles are filtered out of the array rather than hidden, so this is insurance, not a present bug.)

### 2. `frontend/src/graph/Canvas.tsx:136-173` and the commit message — the explanation says three things that are not true

- *"`nodesInitialized` is that fact — false until every tile has handle bounds"* — false; see probe row 4.
- *"The asking stops the moment the library says it has measured"* — it never stops.
- *"It is a timer rather than an animation frame because a browser produces no frames while nothing is changing"* — `useUpdateNodeInternals` itself defers the whole update to `requestAnimationFrame` (`react:3940`), so the fix already rides on a frame; the timer supplies only the repetition. (`setInterval` is throttled in a background tab too, so it is not the escape the sentence implies.)

This is Kent's second veto — not knowing why it did that — and the house rule that a word must mean what it says. Fix the words in the same change as the code, and fix the commit message when the branch is re-committed.

---

## SHOULD FIX

### 3. One rule, not two: the sockets can be declared, exactly as #37 declared the box

`getEdgePosition` falls back to `toHandleBounds(node.handles)` when `internals.handleBounds` is missing, and `isNodeInitialized` (`system:1429`) accepts `node.handles?.length` together with `node.initialWidth`. So if `toFlow` gave each tile its `handles` the way it already gives it `initialWidth`/`initialHeight`, **the wires would be drawable on the first frame with no measurement and no polling at all**, and the file would carry one rule — *every tile is told its box and where its sockets sit, from the one place that worked them out* — instead of a declaration plus a repair loop. It would also be pinnable by a pure-data vitest test in the shape of `src/graph/__tests__/measured.test.ts`, and it matches `spec/workbench/layout-and-zoom.md:50` ("never measured off the screen — so layout stays a pure function").

Two honest caveats, which is why I am not making this a must-fix: the socket geometry lives only in `tile.css:477-494` (8 × 6 px, `left/right: -8px`, `top: 38%`/`62%`, `translateY(-50%)`), so declaring it in TypeScript duplicates a number unless the CSS is driven from the same constants; and `parseHandles` (`system:1639-1647`) rebuilds bounds from the declared handles on **every** `adoptUserNodes`, so a wrong declared offset would move a wire's ends on every hover, not just once. Worth putting to Kent as a design choice rather than deciding here.

### 4. No component-level test pins the rule; one is practical

The diff adds no vitest test. Existing tests already render inside `ReactFlowProvider` (`src/graph/wires/__tests__/causalWire.test.tsx`, `src/components/__tests__/tile.test.tsx`), so a jsdom test that renders `<ReactFlow>` with nodes carrying `measured` and asserts the asking **stops** is straightforward — and it fails on the code as it stands, which is exactly the pin this needs. If the fix goes the way of item 3 instead, the test is pure data and even simpler.

### 5. `frontend/e2e/hormuz.spec.ts:389` — on the ordinary path only one arrow is ever checked

Outside the new shimmed test, the only arrow asserted to be on the glass is `H->C`, through `openThePanelOnTheArrow` at line 863. A different vanished arrow would still go unnoticed in an ordinary cold run. Add the eight-by-name assertion (the one already written at lines 970-980) right after `waitForTheLayout(page, 7)` in the stored-example test — it costs nothing and closes the blind spot for every run, not just the shimmed one.

### 6. For the rebase with `feat/04a-growth`

- That branch's `nodes` memo uses `flatMap` and **drops** tiles with no position yet (`feat-04a-growth/frontend/src/graph/Canvas.tsx:276-309`), so `everyTile` built from `drawing.nodes` will name tiles that are not on the glass. Harmless (`useUpdateNodeInternals` skips ids it cannot find in the DOM) but the docstring's "Every tile on the glass" stops being true. Build the list from the `nodes` the surface actually hands over.
- Every arriving claim changes `drawing`, so the effect restarts and fires one immediate forced re-measure of the whole map per arrival — on top of the permanent poll. That branch's own comment at `Canvas.tsx:450-454` calls re-delivering sizes per arrival *"the storm that starved the drawing library's own measuring"*. Fixing item 1 removes the poll; the per-arrival re-measure is fine and probably wanted.

### 7. `Canvas.tsx:194-197` — `everyTile` churns more than it needs to

`drawing` is recomputed whenever `heights` changes (opening or closing a branch), so `everyTile` is a new array even when the identifiers are identical, and the effect restarts. Comparing the joined identifiers, or keying the memo on something stable, would make the comment "held still so that the asking does not restart on every render" true in more cases.

---

## NITS

- `Canvas.tsx:159` — `useHandlesTheLibraryHasMeasured` uses the drawing library's word. `spec/vocabulary.md:73` says the project's word for where a wire attaches is **port**, and `tiles-ports-wires.md` calls them sockets on screen. The docstring does explain "handle", so this is house-style rather than a rule break.
- `Canvas.tsx:169,170` — `[...ids]` copies the array on every call; only the `readonly` type needs it.
- `e2e/hormuz.spec.ts:305-311` — "the waiting is gone" overstates it: `toHaveCount` is auto-retrying and still waits, up to the config's 15 s `expect.timeout`. The comment's "fifteen seconds" is right; the sentence before it is not.
- `frontend/playwright.config.ts` on this branch still uses fixed ports 8015/5187 with `reuseExistingServer`. Lesson 18's fix rides on `feat/04a-growth`, so whoever runs this branch's last repeat bar must not run it as-is — a bar is on those ports in this worktree right now.

---

## What I checked and found sound

**Proved by reading the installed library:**

- **The root cause is right.** `EdgeWrapper` returns `null` — no `.react-flow__edge` element at all — when `getEdgePosition` is null (`react:2974`), and `getEdgePosition` is null when a node has no handle bounds and no declared handles (`system:1424-1440`). Handle bounds are written only by `updateNodeInternals`, reached either from the `ResizeObserver` (`react:2147-2171`) or from `useUpdateNodeInternals`; the `Handle` component registers nothing itself. So "tiles all present, arrows gone" is exactly the signature of a dropped tile notification, and #37's `initialWidth`/`initialHeight` is precisely why the tiles stay visible while the wires do not.
- **Nothing already placed moves.** Positions come from our own layout and `updateAbsolutePositions` recomputes them identically; the node extent is infinite so nothing is clamped; `NodeWrapper`'s inline size comes from `node.width/height`, not from `measured` (`react:2360-2365`). A forced re-measure cannot make anything jump.
- **Unmount is clean.** The interval is cleared; the in-flight `requestAnimationFrame` inside `useUpdateNodeInternals` is harmless because the store action early-returns with no viewport element.
- **No ResizeObserver feedback loop.** The forced updates do not change any element's size, so they cannot feed the observer. (They do add load, which is item 1's concern, not a loop.)
- **No fight with the keyboard rule from #36/#37.** The poll re-renders `NodeWrapper` but React keeps the same DOM element, so focus is never dropped to the page and `mayLandAgain` is never put in the "nowhere" state by it. Read, not run in a browser.

**Proved by running:**

- `npx biome check src/graph/Canvas.tsx e2e/hormuz.spec.ts` — clean.
- `npx vitest run src/graph` — 13 files, 114 tests, green.
- The `adoptUserNodes` probe above.

**Checked and found in order:**

- The new end-to-end test is deterministic and would be red without the fix: its shim drops every tile's notification and keeps the glass's, so with no repair path no handle bounds are ever written and all eight edges are absent. It asserts both the count and the eight arrows **by name**, so "some arrows drew" cannot pass.
- The old tolerance in `openThePanelOnTheArrow` — the loop that swallowed "the arrow was not on the glass at all" for 45 s — is genuinely gone and replaced by a named assertion.
- No spec chapter or `ARCHITECTURE.md` sentence is made false by this change. #37's rule was never written into the spec (it lives only in `toFlow.ts`'s comment and `measured.test.ts`), so nothing about handles needs a chapter today. If item 3 is taken, `spec/workbench/tiles-ports-wires.md` §"The ports" deserves one sentence saying the sockets' places are declared, not discovered.
- The branch is one commit on `48eb562`, the worktree is clean, and it touches only the two files RESUME lists.

**What I did not do:** no browser, no Playwright, no repeat bar, no whole suite; I did not measure the wall-clock or CPU cost of the poll, only proved that it runs forever and counted the DOM work per tick.</result>

```ts
// that looks at handle bounds at all — see the library's own selector.
```

This is Kent's second veto — not knowing why it did that — and the house rule that a word must mean what it says. Fix the words in the same change as the code, and fix the commit message when the branch is re-committed.

The diff adds no vitest test. `drawing` is recomputed whenever `heights` changes (opening or closing a branch), so `everyTile` is a new array even when the identifiers are identical, and the effect restarts. input.prompt:
```</result>
You are digest analyst FINANCE. Read `/Users/kentgang/git3/katalyst/plans/briefs/05-review-digest-common.md` first, fully — it is your brief's first half and it binds you. Your lens: **stack 05, the thesis — how the map becomes something a trader can act on.** Not one line of it exists yet, so unlike the other analysts you are designing on open ground: the cheapest moment to get it right.

YOUR READING (beyond the common list): `plans/review2/audit-E-finance-thesis.md`, `plans/review2/research-B-quant-finance.md`, `plans/review2/03-engine-and-finance-design.md` §2–§3 (Quantity terminals and Impact edges, price paths, the Position lens with first-touch stop and target, the inverse query by lift, shocks, priced-in and edge, sizing, the thesis card); `plans/review/07-finance-audit.md`, `plans/review/03-independent-finance.md`, `plans/review/09-worked-quantitative-alternative.md` (its conditional-versus-unconditional trade example), `plans/review/10-proposed-change-plan.md` (the thesis parts). Then what exists today: `spec/thesis/README.md` (a landing page only), decision records 0010 (grounding sources: Polymarket and FRED) and 0013 (a payoff names the trade; a quote names the price), `PRODUCT_REQUIREMENTS.md` — every FR and invariant about the thesis, the stop-loss (INV-14), tails, market beliefs, export; `backend/src/katalyst/domain/proposition.py` (`ContractPayoff`, `PricePayoff`), `backend/src/katalyst/fixtures/hormuz.py` (the endings M1, M2 and what they name), `backend/src/katalyst/grounding/` (an empty package), and the present plan for stack 05 in `plans/roadmap-03-to-06.md`.

READ THE BRIEF'S WORDS CLOSELY (`ASSIGNMENT.md`): which clauses actually need a POSITION (an instrument, a side, an entry, a stop, a target), which need only a ranked list of what is tradeable, and which the roadmap's present stack 05 would and would not satisfy. review2 counts "zero lines of code" against three clauses; check its clause-by-clause table yourself.

THE QUESTIONS YOU MUST ANSWER.
1. **The conditional-versus-unconditional trap.** Both reviews warn: "model minus market equals edge" is wrong when the model's number assumes the hypothesis is true and the market's quote spans every outcome. MEASURE, DON'T ASSERT. From the real recording and the kept runs, compute with a small script: is the map a pure tree (every claim exactly one parent)? how many cross-links, how many arrows that push DOWN (inhibitors), how many claims that would falsify an ending, depth, the share of claims that are endings, how many base rates kept and how thin (`0/1`, `1/2`), seconds to the FIRST accepted claim and to a first complete chain from hypothesis to an ending (both reviews say: measure time to first useful output, not total time). review2 claims `ClaimProposal`'s single `cause` field is WHY the map is a tree — but a `LinkProposal` shape exists for arrows between existing claims; find out how often the walk actually asks for or gets one.

1. **Kent's direction for generation is: conditional elicitation, skeleton-first, a small ensemble for numbers** (the common brief). This partly reverses his own earlier decisions — G1/record 0015 (no ensemble), record 0006 (one proposal per call), G7 (up to 25 searches per claim), G4 (three silent retries). For each element, say what the cheapest faithful version is, what it costs (sessions, lines, dollars per map, seconds to first tile and to a finished map), which records it amends, and what it would do to the things that already work and that Kent prizes: reject-never-repair, every refusal visible as an event, provenance decided by us from what the search tool actually returned, the recording/replay format, the one walk-driver. review2's sketch: one streamed structured call drafts the whole DAG (multi-parent, at least one inhibitor and one falsifier per tradeable ending), per-element accept/refuse events ("one DECISION per proposal" instead of "one CALL per proposal"), parallel enrichment per edge on the cheaper model, k = 5 samples per number with the geometric mean of odds, one red-team call; ~3 minutes and ~$0.70 a map. 2. **If the engine moves to conditional numbers** (`q0 = P(B | not A)`, `q1 = P(B | A)` per arrow instead of a log-odds strength; analyst ENGINE is weighing it) — what changes in `proposal.py`, the prompt and the validator, and is it cheap to make the proposal shapes ready for it NOW? This matters today: a fix in flight (making the payoff `kind` required) already changes the answer shapes, which moves the prompt fingerprint and forces a paid re-recording of Hormuz (~$4, ~40 minutes). **If stack 05 or 06 will change the shapes again, say so, and say whether the Hormuz re-recording should simply WAIT for that** rather than be paid for twice. Kent has limited recordings to Hormuz and is concerned about how long paid runs take.
3. **Evidence that means something.** review/: a returned URL proves only that the page appeared in a search, not that it supports the probability, the timing or the instrument; attach a passage or locator, its role, and why it is relevant; check the trade-critical sources of the showcase by hand. What is the smallest change to `SourceDraft`/`Source` and the Inspector that gets most of this, and does it belong in stack 05 (grounding) or later?
4. **Evaluation.** Today: four structural cases and a scorecard (unmerged). Both reviews want a small content rubric (8–12 cases: resolvable? mechanism specific? source supports the claim? DAG not tree? priced-in? observation versus intervention?). Who grades — a person, a model, both — what it costs per round, and where it goes (stack 07 has the pastcast; is a rubric better value than a pastcast?).
5. **Use case 1 ("is A → B reasonable?") as a real search** — forward from A and backward from B — against today's Verify door.
6. **The interactive verbs** — add an event, expand this claim, challenge this arrow — against the roadmap's stack 06 (`refine` with its adds-back-up invariant INV-10, role-played experts, a random-simulation probe, feedback-loop unrolling). review2 says cut `refine`, reflexive loops and probes from version one. What of stack 06 survives, and what is it now FOR?

Then write the generation parts of stacks 05–07 as a plan: what is done, in what order, in which stack, with costs; and what is explicitly NOT done and why.

6. **Stack 07 ("make it presentable")** — README walkthrough, a pastcast self-test, an accessibility sweep, a "what I would do next" page. What stays, what moves earlier, what goes.
```

## 3. The walk driver

**It is `grow.py`, not `following.py`.** `following.py` never decides anything — its contract is "Never decide anything about a map, and never call a model. It reads a walk" (following.py:16). Its loop is:

```python
# following.py:87-98
        try:
            for step in walking:
                if isinstance(step, Finished):
                    self.finished = step
                    break
                self._fold(step)
                if not makes_an_event(step):
                    continue
                yield growth_event(step, self.at - 1)
        except Exception:
            logging.getLogger(__name__).exception(...)
            self.broke = WENT_WRONG
```

### The real loop — `grow()` at `engine/grow.py:124`
1. `start_the_map(hypothesis, is_the_hypothesis=True, ...)` via `_keep_asking` (up to `caps.refusals_in_a_row` = 3 attempts, none told why the last failed) — grow.py:175-201.
2. Optional second `start_the_map(target, is_the_hypothesis=False, ...)` — grow.py:213-230. **The destination never joins the frontier** (comment at grow.py:227-228).
3. The round loop — grow.py:232-274:
```python
    with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=caps.at_once) as pool:
        while not walk.stopped and walk.frontier:
            if len(graph.propositions) >= caps.claims:
                walk.the_map_is_full()
                break
            room = caps.claims - len(graph.propositions)
            asking = list(walk.frontier[: min(caps.at_once, room)])
            walk.watch(answerer)
            answers = _ask_about_each(pool, graph, asking, target=target, answerer=answerer, on=on,
                                      searches_left=caps.searches - walk.receipt.searches)
            walk.bill(answers)
            waiting = list(zip(asking, answers, strict=True))
            while waiting:
                claim_id, answer = waiting.pop(0)
                graph, outcome = walk.fold(graph, claim_id, answer)
                try:
                    yield outcome.model_copy(update={"frontier": tuple(walk.frontier)})
                except GeneratorExit:
                    ...
```
4. Last ending-only pass — grow.py:279-294: `expand(..., ending_only=True)` per line in `_lines_with_no_ending`, folded with `growing=False`.
5. One `Finished` with `_why_it_stopped` (grow.py:809-832): `spend_cap` > `no_terminal` > whatever closed the last open claim (`claim_cap`/`depth_cap`/`width_cap`/`refusal_cap`) > `reached_terminal`.

### Next-step decision
Frontier is a plain FIFO list. `open_a_line` appends (grow.py:374-377); an accepted claim joins it only if non-terminal:
```python
# grow.py:441-450
            arrived = result.proposition
            if growing and arrived is not None and arrived.kind not in TERMINAL_KINDS:
                self.open_a_line(arrived.id, layer=self.layer[claim_id] + 1)
            if growing:
                self._close_if_out_of_room(graph, claim_id)
                if arrived is not None and arrived.id in self.frontier:
                    self._close_if_out_of_room(graph, arrived.id)
```
Lines close on: `Stopped` (grow.py:420-422, reason `"ended"`), 3 refusals in a row (grow.py:430-434), depth cap, width cap (grow.py:501-516), or `the_map_is_full`.

### Does it ever request a `LinkProposal` / cross-link?

**During the walk: it never *asks* for one specifically, but it will accept one, because every expand call sends the `OneProposal` union.** The only thing that mentions cross-links to the model is the standing text (prompt.py:136-141):
```
What an answer is.
Exactly one of three things:
  a new claim, together with the one arrow that reaches it from a claim already
  on the map;
  an arrow between two claims that are both already on the map;
  or a note that this part of the story is finished, with one sentence saying
  why.
```
`expanding_question` (prompt.py:362-443) never narrows to or toward a link; when the claim is near the start with no step yet it actually pushes the *other* way via `ASK_FOR_A_STEP_FIRST` (prompt.py:436-437, 446-455).

**The dispatch** — `expand.py:122-132`:
```python
    if said.declined is not None:
        return costing(Refused(claim_in_words=said.declined), frontier, said)

    proposed = said.answered
    if proposed is None or isinstance(proposed, StartingClaim):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words="The model gave no answer to this question."), frontier, said
        )
    if isinstance(proposed, Stop):
        return costing(Stopped(why=proposed.why), frontier, said)
    return costing(_judge(graph, proposed, found_in(said, on=on)), frontier, said)
```
i.e. anything that is a `ClaimProposal` **or** a `LinkProposal` falls through to `_judge`. The link branch is `expand.py:256-264`:
```python
    if isinstance(proposal, LinkProposal):
        arrow, dropped = _arrow(proposal.link, proposal.source, proposal.target, found)
        return (
            graph.model_copy(update={"links": (*graph.links, arrow)}),
            None,
            (arrow,),
            dropped,
            None,
        )
```
A link-only acceptance then has `result.proposition is None`, so `grow.fold` adds nothing to the frontier and the claim it was asked about stays open (or closes by width).

**The only place a `LinkProposal` is *required*** is `expand_toward` (expand.py:537-592), reachable only from `add_a_claim` (expand.py:448-534), which is the "Add a claim" edit — reached from `record.py:330` (scripted intervention) and the insert API route, **not** from `grow()`:
```python
# expand.py:570-591
    if not isinstance(proposed, LinkProposal):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words=("This call asked for one arrow between two claims already on the "
                                    "map, and the answer was something else.")), added, said)
    if added not in (proposed.source, proposed.target):
        return costing(
            Refused(claim_in_words=("This arrow does not touch the claim that was just added, so it "
                                    "is not part of adding it.")), added, said)
```

**Where a deliberate walk-time cross-link request would go:** a new branch in `grow()`'s round loop (around grow.py:243-253) choosing a different `expand_*` call, plus a new varying-half builder in `prompt.py` beside `joining_question` (prompt.py:312-359 — which already does exactly this shape of ask), plus a dispatch arm in `expand.py`. Nothing today selects candidate pairs.

---

## 4. `prompt.py`

**Assembly.** Two halves. Standing half = the module constant `STANDING_TEXT` (prompt.py:47-146), sent byte-identical as `STANDING_BLOCK` (client.py:141-151) with `"cache_control": {"type": "ephemeral"}`. Varying half = one of four builders, always sent as the single user message:
- `starting_question(sentence, *, is_the_hypothesis, today)` — prompt.py:188
- `adding_question(graph, sentence, *, today)` — prompt.py:264
- `joining_question(graph, added, *, today)` — prompt.py:312
- `expanding_question(graph, frontier, *, target, ending_only, today)` — prompt.py:362

Each starts with `_today(today)` (prompt.py:530) and, where a map is shown, `_map_as_text(graph)` (prompt.py:501-527): claims sorted by id as `  {id}  {claim}` (+ `" (this is what the person expects)"` for the hypothesis), then arrows sorted by `(source, target, id)` as `  {source} -> {target}`. **No likelihoods are shown** ("A model shown its own earlier numbers anchors on them", prompt.py:511-513).

**Prompt fingerprint** — `prompt_hash()` at prompt.py:154:
```python
    from katalyst.engine.client import what_goes_out

    shapes = json.dumps(what_goes_out(), sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"))
    return hashlib.sha256((STANDING_TEXT + shapes).encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()
```
`what_goes_out()` (client.py:188-203) returns `{"proposal": wire_schema(OneProposal), "starting_claim": wire_schema(StartingClaim)}`, where `wire_schema` is `transform_schema(TypeAdapter(shape).json_schema())` (client.py:206-222) — i.e. **the schema as the library actually transmits it**, so every field description and every docstring is inside the hash (see the warning at client.py:180-185: a docstring edit "invalidates every cassette and changes the prompt's fingerprint").

It deliberately **excludes the varying half** (prompt.py:168-170) — so map contents, today's date and the target never change it.

Used at: `following.py:194` (on the live `Receipt` event), `record.py:573` (`KeptRun.prompt_hash`), `record.py:615` (recording header), `record.py:868` and `check_recordings.py:38,45` (fault check), compared at `replay.py:664`.

**Which sections mention what**
- **Base rates / outside view**: `STANDING_TEXT` "Start from the outside, then come inside." (prompt.py:85-98) — "**Search for it.**… Stop searching as soon as you have a countable set with a page behind it… A count you cannot point at a page for is worse than no count". Also `starting_question` prompt.py:250-253 and `adding_question` prompt.py:305-307.
- **Causes / parents**: `STANDING_TEXT` prompt.py:143-145 ("You never name a new claim with anything but its words. The short names in the map we show you are ours; point at one when you name a cause"); `expanding_question` prompt.py:405-406 ("use one when you name a cause"); `joining_question` prompt.py:348-350 ("It may cause something already on the map, or something already on the map may cause it"). "Parents", plural, never appears.
- **Inhibitors / falsifiers / necessary conditions / blockers**: **absent from the entire codebase.** A grep for `inhibit|falsif|parent|necessary condition|blocker` across `src/katalyst/**.py` returns only unrelated branch-`parent` hits in `worlds.py`/`patch.py`/`hormuz.py` and `Path.parents`. Direction of push is carried only by the sign of `LinkDraft.strength` and by `mode`.
- **Endings/trade**: prompt.py:122-133; **citations**: prompt.py:110-116; **claim standing alone**: prompt.py:69-76.

---

## 5. `expand.py` — validation, refusals, reason codes

No split modules. Entry points:
- `expand(graph, frontier, *, target, answerer, on, may_search, ending_only)` — expand.py:76. One walk step.
- `start_the_map(sentence, *, is_the_hypothesis, answerer, on, may_search)` — expand.py:135.
- `add_a_claim(graph, sentence, *, answerer, on, width, may_search, dollars)` — expand.py:448. One `_drafted` call + up to `width` `expand_toward` calls.
- `expand_toward(...)` — expand.py:537. One cross-link between existing claims.
- Minters: `_starting_claim` (192), `_claim` (282), `_arrow` (334).
- Graph helpers used by `grow.py`: `map_with` (374), `still_legal_on` (397), `newly_wrong` (415).

**Where proposals are validated** — `_judge`, expand.py:215-238:
```python
    candidate, claim, arrows, dropped, no_class = _candidate_map(graph, proposal, found)
    introduced = newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))
    if introduced:
        return Refused(claim_in_words=_in_the_models_words(proposal), violations=introduced)
    return Accepted(proposition=claim, links=arrows, sources_dropped=dropped, base_rate_dropped=no_class)
```

`proposal.py` itself holds **no pipeline**. Its only executable logic is `Ranged._range_is_ordered` (proposal.py:94-113). The accept/refuse pipeline, in order:

1. **Shape** — `messages.parse` against `OneProposal`/`StartingClaim`; a miss raises `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` (client.py:481-482) → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:110-120).
2. **Vendor decline** — `Said.declined` → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:122-123).
3. **Wrong shape for the call** — `None`/`StartingClaim` on an expand (expand.py:126-129); non-`LinkProposal` or non-touching link on a join (expand.py:570-591).
4. **`Stop`** → `Stopped`, which is *not* a refusal and puts **no event on the wire** (expand.py:130-131; transcript.py:215-222).
5. **Mint** — `_claim` (id, `Belief(..., owner="model")`, base-rate citation filter) and `_arrow` (id, day-widened lag/half-life, `keep_cited`, `provenance_of`, `reflexive=False` always) — expand.py:282-371.
6. **Map rules** — `newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))` → `Refused(violations=...)` or `Accepted` (expand.py:232-238).
7. **Re-judge at the fold** — `still_legal_on` then the width cap → possibly a late `Refused` (grow.py:455-499).

## 9. `proposal.py` — the "validator pipeline"

`proposal.py` itself holds **no pipeline**. Its only executable logic is `Ranged._range_is_ordered` (proposal.py:94-113). Everything else is shape-as-constraint; the module docstring is explicit (proposal.py:38-40): *"If you find yourself writing a check that the model did not do one of the three, the shape is wrong."*

The accept/refuse pipeline, in order:

1. **Shape** — `messages.parse` against `OneProposal`/`StartingClaim`; a miss raises `AnswerWeCouldNotRead` (client.py:481-482) → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:110-120).
2. **Vendor decline** — `Said.declined` → `Refused` with no violations (expand.py:122-123).
3. **Wrong shape for the call** — `None`/`StartingClaim` on an expand (expand.py:126-129); non-`LinkProposal` or non-touching link on a join (expand.py:570-591).
4. **`Stop`** → `Stopped`, which is *not* a refusal and puts **no event on the wire** (expand.py:130-131; transcript.py:215-222).
5. **Mint** — `_claim` (id, `Belief(..., owner="model")`, base-rate citation filter) and `_arrow` (id, day-widened lag/half-life, `keep_cited`, `provenance_of`, `reflexive=False` always) — expand.py:282-371.
6. **Map rules** — `newly_wrong(validate(graph), validate(candidate))` → `Refused(violations=...)` or `Accepted` (expand.py:232-238).
7. **Re-judge at the fold** — `still_legal_on` then the width cap → possibly a late `Refused` (grow.py:455-499).

**Event types emitted per proposal** — `events.growth_event`, events.py:317-346:
```python

    if isinstance(result, Accepted):
        return ProposalAccepted(at=at, proposition=result.proposition, links=result.links, frontier=outcome.frontier)
    if not isinstance(result, Refused):
        raise TypeError(...)
    return ProposalRejected(at=at, claim_in_words=result.claim_in_words, violations=result.violations, frontier=outcome.frontier)
```
